title: Partial pressures along the path of oxygen
body: A student copied the following partial pressures (in mm Hg) from a textbook table while revising gas exchange. Atmospheric air: pO2 159, pCO2 0.3. Alveoli: pO2 104, pCO2 40. Deoxygenated blood: pO2 40, pCO2 45. Oxygenated blood: pO2 95, pCO2 40. Tissues: pO2 40, pCO2 45. The student remembered that O2 and CO2 are exchanged at the alveoli and at the tissues by simple diffusion, mainly along a pressure or concentration gradient, but was unsure in which direction each gas moves at each site. Use these values to decide where each gas moves from and to.
